column1: # r02 ile silinen anlamlar (geri yüklemek için).

column5: to bring something to an end, especially a discussion, event, or piece of work
column6: The professor wrapped up the lecture with a quick recap. / After the interview, she wrapped up her notes and left the office. / The committee wrapped up the voting process by midnight. / He wrapped up the research paper after months of data analysis. / The conference organizers wrapped up the symposium with a panel discussion on future trends.

column5: to pull out or remove the root of a plant or object.
column6: The gardener rooted out the invasive species that threatened the pond. / Officials vowed to root out fraud in the upcoming audit. / Researchers are trying to root out the underlying causes of the disease. / Activists aim to root out systemic bias from institutional policies.

column5: to make someone feel happier or more lively
column6: A funny video cheered up the whole office during lunch. / The bright decorations cheered up the children at the party. / His kind words cheered up the patients in the waiting area. / Music from the band cheered up the crowd after a long day of work. / The unexpected compliment cheered up the shy student during the presentation.

column5: to become less angry, excited, or agitated
column6: He took a deep breath to cool down after the meeting. / The crowd began to cool down once the speaker finished.

column5: to bring a thought, memory, or idea into one's mind, especially suddenly or vividly
column6: The photograph conjured up a feeling of longing in the viewer. / His voice conjured up the atmosphere of a bustling marketplace. / She tried to conjure up a convincing argument for the debate team. / The documentary conjured up powerful images of climate change impacts. / During the therapy session, the patient conjured up suppressed childhood experiences.

column5: to arrange people or objects in a straight sequence or queue
column6: The children lined up quietly before entering the classroom. / Customers lined up outside the store for the Black Friday sale. / Police officers lined up the suspects for questioning. / The participants were asked to line up according to their registration numbers. / During the evacuation drill, everyone had to line up in an orderly fashion.

column5: to appear or become visible suddenly, often unexpectedly
column6: A small stall popped up in the park during the festival. / Unexpected errors popped up while I was editing the document. / A new app popped up on the screen, offering a discount.

column5: to give a brief statement of the main points of something
column6: After the lecture, she will sum up the main ideas for the class. / The report sums up the economic impact of the new policy. / Can you sum up the story in two sentences for the summary? / During the meeting, the manager summed up the quarterly results for the board. / The researcher summed up the complex methodology into a concise paragraph for the journal.
